name: SiT8008BI-21-33E-25.000000
title: SiT8008B: low-power programmable MEMS oscillator, 1 to 110 MHz, LVCMOS output, 1.62 to 3.63 V
summary: A MEMS clock oscillator whose frequency is factory-set to any value from 1 MHz to 110 MHz with six decimal places, giving an LVCMOS/HCMOS square wave from a four-pad package footprint-compatible with quartz oscillators. Ordering codes choose the supply (1.8, 2.5, 2.8, 3.0 or 3.3 V, or a wide 2.25 to 3.63 V or 1.62 to 3.63 V range), the overall stability (±20, ±25 or ±50 ppm), the temperature range, the output edge speed, the function of pin 1 (output enable, standby or none) and one of five package sizes from 2.0 x 1.6 mm to 7.0 x 5.0 mm. SiT8008BI-21-33E-25.000000 is the 25 MHz part, industrial -40 to +85 °C, ±20 ppm, 3.3 V supply, pin 1 as output enable, default drive, in the 3.2 x 2.5 mm package, shipped in bulk.

pins.name: OE/ST/NC
pins.function: Pin 1, set at the factory to one of three functions. Output enable (OE): high runs the specified output; low puts the output in high impedance, only the output driver being turned off. Standby (ST, active low): high runs the output; low puts the device to sleep with the output weakly pulled low and the supply current at I_std. No connect (NC): the output runs whatever the voltage on pin 1, anywhere from 0 to Vdd or open.

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Supply. Needs a capacitor of 0.1 µF or more to GND.

notes: Pin 1 in the OE or ST function: when nothing drives it, a pull-up of 10 kΩ or less is recommended; a pin 1 that must float calls for the NC function.

circuits.title: Test circuit
circuits.description: The set-up under which the output figures are measured. A power supply feeds VDD with 0.1 µF across it to ground; the output drives 15 pF to ground, a figure that counts the probe and fixture, and is measured at a test point. For the OE or ST function, pin 1 is tied up to Vdd through 1 kΩ.

equations.name: Maximum frequency for a rise/fall time

where.Trf_20/80: typical 20 % to 80 % rise/fall time from the rise/fall time vs CLOAD tables

equations.note: The highest frequency at which full output swing is guaranteed across the whole operating temperature range for that drive setting and load. Worked case: Vdd = 1.8 V, 30 pF load, 3 ns wanted, drive code E, fMAX = 66.666660 MHz, part number SiT8008BIE12-18E-66.666660.

where.TH: time the output spends above 50 % of Vdd in one cycle

operation.text: Pin 1 is set at the factory, or by the Time Machine on field-programmable parts, to output enable (OE), standby (ST, active low) or no connect (NC). In OE a low level turns off only the output driver, leaving it high impedance while the core keeps running; current falls because the output is idle, and on a high level the output comes back, typically in under 1 µs. In ST a low level shuts every internal circuit down and the current drops to a few µA typical; a high level starts a resume that takes up to 5 ms. In NC the output always runs, whatever level pin 1 sees.

The output is gated: from the first pulse after power-up or after leaving standby it is within the rated stability, with no runt pulses and no glitches. During start-up and resume the output is high impedance. Start-up time counts from Vdd reaching its rated minimum; resume time counts from the ST input crossing 50 % of Vdd. OE enable and disable times count from the OE input crossing 50 % of Vdd.

The output edge rate is chosen with a drive strength code in the part number. Slower edges lower radiated EMI: going from edges of 5 % to 45 % of the period cuts the 11th harmonic by 35 dB. Faster edges reduce the jitter a receiving chip picks up from supply noise, and some receivers need them. A stronger setting keeps full swing and sharp edges into large loads, up to 60 pF or more. A 3.3 V part with the default setting has edges of 1 ns typical into 15 pF, 2.6 ns into 45 pF, and 1.83 ns into 45 pF with a stronger drive setting.

Pick the rise/fall table for the nominal supply (1.8, 2.5, 2.8, 3.0 or 3.3 V), go to the column for the load (5 to 60 pF), find the row giving the wanted edge time, and put that row's letter in the drive strength field of the part number. The default is a dash. Each edge time sets a highest frequency at full swing, 1 / (5 × Trf).
VDD needs a capacitor to GND of 0.1 µF or more.

Field-programmable versions exist in all five package sizes. The Time Machine II, a USB-powered programmer, sets their frequency (1 to 110 MHz), stability (±20, ±25 or ±50 ppm), temperature range (-20 to 70 °C or -40 to 85 °C), supply option (1.8, 2.5, 2.8, 3.0, 3.3 V, 2.25 to 3.63 V or 1.62 to 3.63 V), drive strength and pin 1 function. Volume parts are programmed at the factory to the ordering code.
In the top marking, Y is the manufacturing origin, which depends on the assembly site, and XXXX is the manufacturing lot number.
SiT1618, SiT8918 and SiT8920 cover 125 °C and -55 °C ranges; SiT8924 and SiT8925 are the AEC-Q100 versions; SiT8944 is offered for aerospace and defense.
